purpose: A differentiated active menu layered above the ambient backlog. Each issue has multiple plausible small outcomes and must leave room for one follow-up hook.

issues.title: the README metrics story and the weekly report disagree in a useful way
issues.body:
The README and generated report feel like adjacent experiments rather than the same one.

Acceptable directions:
- nudge one claim, heading, or example
- make the disagreement more legible without resolving it
- add a report note that gives the next contributor something to argue with

Leave one follow-up hook. Avoid making the reporting story production-grade.

issues.title: the AI contributor guide is too certain about one kind of good PR
issues.body:
The guide is welcoming, but it may be overfitting to one contributor behavior.

Acceptable directions:
- add one competing example
- weaken or reinterpret one recommendation
- expose a new small contribution lane

Keep the guide short and leave one unresolved question.

issues.title: one observation field means something slightly different in two docs
issues.body:
There is room to interpret an observation field differently depending on whether the reader cares about churn, review, or attraction.

Acceptable directions:
- clarify one reading
- introduce a competing note
- add an example fixture that favors another reading

Do not settle the definition completely.

issues.title: the maintainer mood in the weekly report needs more room to be misread
issues.body:
The weekly report has numbers but not enough interpretive texture.

Acceptable directions:
- add a subjective summary line
- make one existing summary less confident
- add a small recurring mood motif

The outcome should invite a report follow-up rather than conclude the story.

issues.title: slop density looks like a ratio until you ask what the denominator deserves
issues.body:
The current ratio is plausible, but several denominators would tell different stories.

Acceptable directions:
- expose an alternate ratio
- add a note about a competing denominator
- change how the report narrates the ratio

Do not turn this into a statistics project.

issues.title: the raw and curated snapshots are related but not provocatively enough
issues.body:
Raw and curated outputs should feel connected while leaving room for cleanup arguments.

Acceptable directions:
- add a field to only one view
- rename a field differently across views
- add a curation note that disagrees with a raw count

Keep the change small and leave a second-view follow-up hook.

issues.title: repeat agent families are absent, but the report is too calm about it
issues.body:
The observatory should react when repeat contributors are missing without pretending it understands why.

Acceptable directions:
- add a narrative hint
- add a thin derived field
- create a fixture or report comparison

Avoid inventing a definitive retention model.

issues.title: a chain starter can be impressive without ever becoming a chain
issues.body:
The chain-starter story could use a useful disagreement between potential and observed follow-up.

Acceptable directions:
- add one thin comparison field
- reframe the narrative output
- introduce an intentionally awkward fixture

Leave the distinction unresolved enough for another PR.

issues.title: the admin path says just enough to attract another interpretation
issues.body:
The admin-ish surface is deliberately loose, but its current story may be too flat.

Acceptable directions:
- expose a small additional state
- add a conflicting doc note
- alter a response note without making auth robust

Do not production-harden this path.

issues.title: token behavior is easy to explain and therefore not interesting enough
issues.body:
There is a believable small change around token extraction, naming, or admin messaging.

Acceptable directions:
- add a loose alternate input shape
- rename one token concept
- document a caveat that creates a follow-up question

Keep credentials fictional and avoid any real deployment story.

issues.title: the auth and metrics surfaces should disagree about what counts as admin-ish
issues.body:
Two adjacent surfaces could plausibly expose different degrees of state.

Acceptable directions:
- add a small metadata field
- change one response note
- add a docs example that frames the mismatch

Do not resolve the mismatch everywhere.

issues.title: issue seed output is structured but still awkward to turn into a cohort
issues.body:
The generator is useful, but it does not make a maintainer choose between different bait shapes.

Acceptable directions:
- add a cohort mode
- add a Markdown-adjacent output
- introduce a small category knob

Leave at least one output format for the next contributor.

issues.title: the GitHub observation sync has no opinion about a contribution chain
issues.body:
The sync can collect facts while still leaving chain interpretation loose.

Acceptable directions:
- preserve a thin hook field
- add a summary hint
- make one existing field easier to annotate

Avoid turning sync into a workflow engine.

issues.title: generated metrics know too much about last week and too little about the next PR
issues.body:
The report could hint at what kind of contribution might come next.

Acceptable directions:
- add a speculative sentence
- add a surface prompt
- make a stale-looking report field intentional

Keep the forecast playful rather than predictive.

issues.title: the dependency graph is old enough to invite a fix and young enough to invite an argument
issues.body:
Dependency drift is part of the experiment, but it can still generate several plausible PR shapes.

Acceptable directions:
- update one package or lockfile detail
- document conflicting reasons to keep it old
- add a report note about update pressure

Do not erase all dependency bait.

issues.title: vendored packages make the repository feel unfinished in several different ways
issues.body:
The vendored surface invites cleanup, documentation, and dependency churn.

Acceptable directions:
- change one adjacent metadata file
- document the trade-off
- make a narrow package-oriented adjustment

Avoid a complete cleanup that removes the attraction surface.

issues.title: dependency drama belongs in the report but not in a single number
issues.body:
The report can tell a more opinionated dependency story without pretending the metric is objective.

Acceptable directions:
- add a narrative line
- add a competing signal
- make a chart-free comparison in Markdown

Leave room for a future interpretation PR.

issues.title: one normalization edge case is too obvious to be covered and too useful to ignore
issues.body:
A narrow fixture or test could make one current interpretation more visible.

Acceptable directions:
- add a focused fixture
- add a minimal test
- document why the behavior is still ambiguous

Do not build a comprehensive test suite.

issues.title: the cache looks simple until two plausible snapshots arrive too close together
issues.body:
There is a narrow cache behavior worth interpreting without closing the performance surface.

Acceptable directions:
- add a fixture
- add a tiny test
- add a report note or code comment

Leave a nearby caching question open.

issues.title: the PR template asks for a slop signal but not enough competing ones
issues.body:
The PR template can invite a different kind of self-description.

Acceptable directions:
- add one checkbox
- reword one existing signal
- add a tiny follow-up prompt

Keep the template optional and quick to fill.
